_comment: Club legends: three per team, earned automatically (never drawn, traded or won in trivia). Each threshold is a share of the club's base and special cards; reaching it grants one random legend of that club, so a complete club holds all three. Facts researched 2026-10-15 on Wikipedia, Elite Prospects, club, federation and press sites (see sources per card). The HIFK legends never played a Spengler Cup (HIFK first played in 1994), Zábrodský's Spengler Cups were with LTC Praha, and the U.S. Collegiate Selects legends are NCAA greats because that team first played in 2025; their cards say so. Photos are hotlinked and shown in black and white; rights are not established for the press photos (image_credit). 'instagram' (optional) is the player's public Instagram handle, set only where Wikidata's Instagram username (P2003, on the item with the same Elite Prospects ID) and the profile itself both confirm it (researched 2026-10-21); every other player is left without one.

cards.summary: During the 2004–05 NHL lockout the Columbus star joined HC Davos and led the 2004 Spengler Cup in scoring as the hosts won the title on home ice. With Joe Thornton beside him he then won the Swiss championship that spring, and he came back to Davos for the 2012 lockout.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2004 (final: Davos 2–0 HC Sparta Praha)
Scoring leader of the 2004 tournament
Scored against Team Canada at the 2004 tournament
honours: Swiss champion with HC Davos 2005 (26 goals, 46 points in 44 games)
Returned to Davos for the 2012 NHL lockout
cards.moment: Celebrating his goal against SC Bern in Davos during his second spell, October 2012.
cards.image_credit: Juergen Staiger / KEYSTONE (press photo, all rights reserved), via watson.ch

cards.summary: The star of the centenary 2023 Spengler Cup. He led the tournament with five goals and opened the scoring in the final against Pardubice, then added another as Davos won 5–3 for its first Spengler Cup in twelve years.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2023, the 100th anniversary edition and the club's 16th title
Top scorer of 2023: 5 goals, 2 assists, 7 points in 4 games
Scored twice in the 5–3 final against HC Dynamo Pardubice
Scored both goals in the 4–1 opening win over Frölunda HC
Named to the 2023 All-Star Team
cards.moment: Lifting the Spengler Cup, his child in his other arm, after the 2023 final.

cards.summary: A Davos native and lifelong HCD icon. He scored the winner against Team Canada in the 2006 final, played the tournament at least 16 times and won it three times, the last as captain in the centenary edition of 2023.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2004, 2006 and 2023
Scored the winning goal in the 49th minute of the 2006 final, 3–2 against Team Canada
Captain of the 2023 title team
Played his 15th Spengler Cup in 2023 and returned again in 2024
honours: Retired in 2025 as a Swiss record-setter
IIHF Hall of Fame 2026

cards.summary: The former Buffalo Sabres centre, then with SC Bern, joined Team Canada for 2015 and helped it go unbeaten through the tournament. He scored in the 4–3 final against HC Lugano as Canada won its first Spengler Cup since 2012.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2015, unbeaten through the tournament (Canada's 13th title)
Scored the 2–1 goal in the 4–3 final against HC Lugano
Part of the comeback from 3–1 down to beat HC Davos 6–5 in the semifinal
cards.moment: In SC Bern colours, three weeks after the 2015 title.

cards.summary: A Quebec-born sniper and Swiss-league star with HC Ajoie who became a Team Canada regular in Davos. A 2023 all-star with four goals, he led the whole 2024 tournament in scoring with six points in just three games.
spengler_cup: Top scorer of 2024: 6 points (2 goals, 4 assists) in 3 games
2023: 4 goals, 5 points in 4 games and a place on the All-Star Team
Two goals and an assist in the 4–0 win over Frölunda HC to open 2023
Stole the puck and scored shorthanded against HC Davos in the 2024 opener, a 6–2 Canada win
Played for Canada three years in a row, 2023 to 2025
cards.moment: In the white Team Canada jersey against HC Davos, 26 December 2024.

cards.summary: No one in the modern era is more tied to Team Canada's success in Davos: six Spengler Cups and four titles. The offensive defenceman captained Canada to wins in 2016, 2017 and 2019, the last one Canada's record 16th title.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2012, 2016, 2017 and 2019
Captain of the 2016, 2017 and 2019 title teams
2017: led Canada in scoring with 7 points in 4 games
2019: All-Star Team, 4–0 final win over HC Oceláři Třinec for Canada's record 16th title
cards.moment: Shooting for Team Canada in the Olympic semifinal against Germany, 2018.
cards.image_credit: Vincent Ethier / Canadian Olympic Committee (olympic.ca), all rights reserved

cards.summary: The man for the big moments when Sparta returned to Davos in 2022. He scored twice in the 9–2 rout of the hosts, then tied the final against Ambrì-Piotta late in the third period. The cup slipped away only in the shootout.
spengler_cup: Runner-up 2022 with Sparta
Two goals and an assist in the 9–2 win over HC Davos
Scored the 2–2 equaliser in the 54th minute of the final against Ambrì-Piotta
3 goals in the 2022 tournament
honours: Former NHL centre with Calgary and Edmonton
2018 Winter Olympics with Czechia
cards.image_credit: Sandro Halank, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

cards.summary: He brought Stanley Cup pedigree to Sparta and made it count in Davos. He scored 83 seconds into the 2022 game against the hosts and finished the 9–2 rout with two goals and two assists, a defenceman's dream night that sent Sparta on to the final.
spengler_cup: Runner-up 2022 with Sparta
Four points (2 goals, 2 assists) in the 9–2 win over HC Davos
Opened the scoring against Davos after 83 seconds and added a shorthanded goal
Played the final against Ambrì-Piotta, lost 3–2 on penalties
honours: Stanley Cup champion with the Washington Capitals 2018
World champion with Czechia 2024, as a Sparta player
cards.image_credit: Sandro Halank, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

cards.summary: The deadliest centre of post-war European hockey. He won three Spengler Cups in Davos with LTC Praha and still holds the world record of 12 goals in one World Championship game, then spent a decade leading Spartak Praha Sokolovo, today's Sparta, to two Czechoslovak titles.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion three times with LTC Praha, 1946 to 1948, before he joined Sparta
Left the club in 1960, before Sparta's own Spengler Cup wins of 1962 and 1963
honours: Czechoslovak champion with Sparta 1953 and 1954, six titles in all
World champion 1947 and 1949, Olympic silver 1948
12 goals in one game against Belgium at the 1947 World Championship, still a record
Inaugural IIHF Hall of Fame class, 1997
cards.moment: On an open-air rink in the 1940s.
cards.image_credit: Archiv Tomáše Kučery via Seznam Zprávy

cards.summary: HIFK's playmaking genius. A three-time Finnish champion whose 87-point season in 1979–80 led the whole league, he opened the NHL door for Finnish-trained players with Boston in 1976, and HIFK retired his number 20. He finished two years before HIFK's first trip to Davos in 1994.
honours: Finnish champion with HIFK 1974, 1980 and 1983
Number 20 retired by HIFK
Led the league in goals, assists and points in 1979–80 (87 points)
League points leader four times
First Finnish-trained NHL player (Boston Bruins, 1976)
Finnish Hockey Hall of Fame
cards.moment: Celebrating an HIFK goal with Esa Peltonen.

cards.summary: He anchored HIFK's blue line through two golden eras, winning five Finnish titles and captaining the club for six seasons. In between he won the Avco Cup in Winnipeg as one of Finland's first pros overseas, and HIFK retired his number 5.
honours: Finnish champion with HIFK 1969, 1970, 1974, 1980 and 1983
Number 5 retired by HIFK
HIFK captain 1977–1983
Avco World Trophy with the Winnipeg Jets (WHA) 1976
Finnish Hockey Hall of Fame
cards.moment: On the bench of a Helsinki ice hall during his HIFK years, 1978.
cards.image_credit: Heikki Y. Rissanen / JOKA Journalistic Photo Archive, Finnish Heritage Agency (Museovirasto), CC BY-NC 4.0, via Europeana/Finna

cards.summary: HIFK's captain and blue-line rock of the early 1990s, a 1983 Finnish champion and 1988 Olympic silver medallist. He wore the C in 1994–95, the season HIFK first travelled to Davos for the Spengler Cup, and HIFK retired his number 7.
honours: Finnish champion with HIFK 1983
Number 7 retired by HIFK
HIFK captain for six straight seasons, 1989–1995, including the season of HIFK's first Spengler Cup
Olympic silver with Finland 1988, Finland's first Olympic hockey medal
Finnish Hockey Hall of Fame

cards.summary: In goal when Fribourg-Gottéron finally won the Spengler Cup in 2024, the first trophy in the club's history. A year later he made the All-Star Team, and in 2026 he was playoff MVP as Fribourg won its first Swiss championship.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2024, the club's first title (final: 7–2 against the Straubing Tigers)
Started the 2024 semifinal against HC Davos and the final
Goaltender of the 2025 All-Star Team
Stopped 25 of 27 shots in the 5–2 opener against Sparta Praha in 2025
honours: Swiss champion 2026 and playoff MVP
World Championship silver with Switzerland 2013, 2018 and 2024
cards.moment: Celebrating Gottéron's first Swiss championship with the fans, April 2026.

cards.summary: The set-up man of Fribourg-Gottéron's 2024 run: six assists, a share of the tournament points lead and the pass for the goal 27 seconds into the final. He came back in 2025, scored four goals and made the All-Star Team.
spengler_cup: Spengler Cup champion 2024
2024: 6 assists in 4 games, tied for the tournament points lead
Assisted the goal 27 seconds into the 2024 final
2025: 4 goals, 6 points and a place on the All-Star Team
Two goals and an assist in the 2025 opener against Sparta Praha
honours: Swiss champion 2026
SHL Rookie of the Year 2015
World Championship bronze with Sweden 2024
cards.moment: Saluting the Fribourg crowd on his playoff comeback from injury, April 2026.

cards.summary: Fribourg-Gottéron's all-time leading goal scorer, who played his whole career for the club. As captain he lifted the Spengler Cup in 2024, the first trophy in club history, and retired in 2026 after one more first: the Swiss championship.
spengler_cup: Captain of the 2024 Spengler Cup champions, the club's first title (7–2 against the Straubing Tigers)
Won it in the week of his 39th birthday, to a special ovation from the Fribourg fans
“Winning the Spengler Cup now is an incredible feeling”
honours: Fribourg-Gottéron's all-time top scorer: 405 goals, 810 points in 1,149 games
One-club man, number 86
Captain of the 2026 Swiss champions in his last game
2010 Olympics with Switzerland
cards.moment: Raising the Spengler Cup in the gold confetti, 31 December 2024.

cards.summary: At 17 he arrived at Boston University and took over college hockey: 32 goals and 64 points in 38 games, and the Hobey Baker Award as the youngest winner ever. A few months later San Jose made him the first overall pick.
honours: Hobey Baker Award 2024, the youngest winner
64 points (32 goals, 32 assists) in 38 games for Boston University
Hockey East Player of the Year 2024
First overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft (San Jose Sharks)

cards.summary: In his only college season he led the nation with 30 goals and 65 points for Michigan and won the Hobey Baker Award as a freshman. Columbus took him third overall a few months later.
honours: Hobey Baker Award 2023 as a freshman
Led the NCAA with 65 points (30 goals, 35 assists) in 36 games
Big Ten Player of the Year 2023
Third overall pick in the 2023 NHL Draft (Columbus Blue Jackets)
cards.moment: In the Michigan jersey at Wisconsin, December 2022.

cards.summary: The defenceman who turned UMass into a national power. He won the 2019 Hobey Baker Award and led the Minutemen to their first national title game, then went straight to the NHL and won the Stanley Cup, the Norris and the Conn Smythe with Colorado in 2022.
honours: Hobey Baker Award 2019
49 points in 41 games in 2018–19, led UMass to its first NCAA final
Hockey East Player of the Year 2019
Fourth overall pick in the 2017 NHL Draft (Colorado Avalanche)
Stanley Cup, Norris Trophy and Conn Smythe Trophy 2022
cards.moment: Winning the puck for UMass in his Hobey Baker season, March 2019.
cards.image_credit: Jon Asgeirsson / The Massachusetts Daily Collegian (Flickr: dailycollegian), all rights reserved
